title: Neural mortality prediction matches simpler models after emergency laparotomy
summary: A multilayer perceptron predicted 30-day mortality using 8,293 emergency laparotomy operations in an Australasian audit. Internal test AUROC was 0.817, without a significant advantage over logistic regression or the NELA score. Imputation before splitting could leak information, although complete-case sensitivity analysis gave similar discrimination. This retrospective result does not establish improved surgical decisions or patient outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective internal 80:20 operation-level split, comparison with logistic regression and NELA, and complete-case sensitivity analysis.
evidence.unknown: External clinical utility remains unestablished; pre-split imputation and selection among repeated model runs may inflate performance, and the denominator is operations rather than established unique patients.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks learn relationships between preoperative audit variables and recorded 30-day mortality.
